A bomb-making material that the Army said was unstable and likely to explode on its own.
Eliza Billingham from Iowa Public Radio has more.
The EPA says it has not found any lead in the air or on the ground in communities surrounding the Army's detonation zone.
Major General Eric Shirley credits state-of-the-art mitigation efforts that soldiers put in place to control the blast.
The lead azide barrels were already underground.
The Army added tarps, gel blocks, and two feet of particle-collecting foam around the blast zone.
The EPA has roughly 300 people in place to continue testing air, soil, and surface water for any contamination.
The University of Iowa is also conducting independent sampling.
Those results will be available in a few days.
For NPR News, I'm Eliza Billingham in Iowa City.
The Trump administration is proposing additional tariffs on goods from 13 countries and the European Union.
President Trump rolled out this latest tariff proposal Wednesday as consumer inflation continues to rise following a bruising midterm election for Republicans.
Here's NPR's Danielle Kurtzleben.
The new tariffs would be on some of the U.S.'s largest trading partners, including China and the EU.
The administration says these are proposed tariffs and that they are seeking public comment on the new rates.
For each country, the administration has a proposed tariff rate and what the administration calls a deal rate, a lower rate that they could be willing to impose.
A senior administration official told reporters Tuesday night that the tariffs on Chinese goods would be 20 percent, but could go as high as 40 percent depending on ongoing negotiations.
The new rates come just weeks after Republicans lost dozens of seats in Congress due in part to high prices, which tariffs can exacerbate.
Danielle Kurtzleben, NPR News.
Now to Northern California, several communities there faced evacuation orders Wednesday as flood waters inundated homes and streets.
From Jefferson Public Radio, Theo Greenlee reports.
Residents of the small waterfront community of King Salmon were ordered to evacuate Tuesday as rising water flooded local streets.
But a day later, Eli Blassingame was still in his trailer at a local RV park where he's lived for three years, even as flood waters rose.
It went probably up to my thigh, the water did, so I had to start putting on hip waders because the tide was coming in.
The National Weather Service says unusually high tides, El Nino and strong southerly winds have pushed water levels near historic highs.
Forecasters say flooding remains possible through Friday.
For NPR News, I'm Theo Greenlee in Beaverton.
The original guitarist of the English pop rock band Duran Duran has died.
Andy Taylor was 65 years old. His family says he died Monday after battling prostate cancer.
He revealed that diagnosis in 2022.
Americans getting more comfortable with using A.I. to help plan Thanksgiving dinner.
Here's NPR's Chloe Veltman.
Tomorrow Hancock is among the many chefs on social media testing A.I. recipes ahead of the holidays, like sweet potato blueberry cake.
This one is going to receive a D because this is not a cake at all. This is custard, but it is like sad custard.
Despite the pushback against A.I. slop, Campbell's 2026 Thanksgiving report says close to one in three Americans would trust an A.I. recipe enough to try it for the holidays, even without a test run.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR.
